conf.description: cisco-asa connection-events dataset, netflow (NSEL) format: NSEL is binary NetFlow v9, which Cribl Stream does not natively decode; a NetFlow collector or the Elastic Agent netflow input must terminate and decode the UDP stream before events reach Cribl, and the Elastic NetFlow Records integration owns mapping the decoded elements to ECS. This pipeline is intentionally thin: it only tags event.dataset and passes the (already-decoded) record through untouched.

conf.comment: cisco-asa / connection-events / netflow: NSEL flow-create/flow-teardown records. Per the map there is no packaged ASA-NSEL pack for Cribl and Cribl Stream does not decode binary NetFlow v9, so a NetFlow collector or Elastic Agent netflow input must decode the stream upstream of any Cribl touchpoint. The map's field table renames its columns to the generic vendor mnemonics (NF_F_SRC_ADDR_IPV4, NF_F_FW_EVENT, etc.) rather than the literal JSON keys an upstream decoder would emit, so this pipeline does not attempt field renames here -- doing so would mean guessing key names the map does not specify. All ECS mapping (including the custom NF_F_FW_EVENT/NF_F_FW_EXT_EVENT/ACL-id handling) is left to the Elastic netflow integration and its documented @custom pipeline.
